_note: 科研時事（站點級，跨科目）。顯示在三科總覽頁。cat 用 bio/chem/phys/math，只影響標籤顏色。越新的排越前。內容必須來自可靠來源並附連結——時事不是常識，寧可少寫也不要編。本檔由 scripts/fetch_news.py 自動抓取泛科學 RSS 產生，可手動補充。

items.t: IceCube偵測到的幽靈粒子能量是太陽中微子的100億倍
items.x: 被稱為中微子的神秘粒子不斷地流經我們的身體，科學家現在正在使用埋在南極冰層中的大型天文台來探測來自遙遠宇宙源的極其強大的中微子。這些難以捉摸的「幽靈粒子」可能蘊藏著有關大爆炸、極端宇宙事件以及宇宙中一些最大奧秘的非凡線索。
items.orig: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
items.origX: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. These elusive “ghost particles” could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universe’s greatest mysteries.

items.t: 科學家發現金屬可以抵抗 -424°F 的深度冷凍
items.x: 科學家發現了一種令人驚訝的機制，可以使某些金屬在低至 -253°C (-424°F) 的溫度下抵抗開裂，而此時類似的材料通常會變得非常脆弱。兩種實驗合金沒有斷裂，而是重新組織了內部結構，創造了吸收壓力和保持靈活性的新方法。
items.orig: Scientists discover metals that defy the deep freeze at -424°F
items.origX: Scientists have discovered a surprising mechanism that allows certain metals to resist cracking at temperatures as low as -253°C (-424°F), when similar materials typically become dangerously brittle. Instead of breaking, two experimental alloys reorganize their internal structures, creating new ways to absorb stress and remain flexible.

items.t: 革命性的新型顯微鏡可以揭示隱藏的生命機制
items.x: 研究人員開發了一種革命性的顯微鏡，它使用極其強大的激光，使以前看不見的細胞結構變得更容易看到。該技術極大地提高了影像清晰度，使科學家能夠檢查傳統電子顯微鏡難以捕捉的小蛋白質。它最終可能揭示微小的分子機器如何在細胞內相互作用，前提是
items.orig: A revolutionary new microscope could reveal the hidden machinery of life
items.origX: Researchers have developed a revolutionary microscope that uses an incredibly powerful laser to make previously invisible cellular structures easier to see. The technology dramatically improves image clarity, allowing scientists to examine small proteins that conventional electron microscopes struggle to capture. It could eventually reveal how tiny molecular machines interact inside cells, providing an unprecedented look at the hidden workings of life.

items.t: 科學家發現了一個可以引發或破壞化學反應的隱藏因素
items.x: 研究人員發現了一個可以決定化學反應成功或失敗的隱藏因素，然後利用它將所需產物的比例從 16% 提高到 97%。透過控制電極附近的酸度，他們開發了一種很有前途的方法，使用氧氣和電力而不是添加危險的氧化劑來製造塑膠、藥品和其他產品的化學物質。
items.orig: Scientists discover a hidden factor that can make or break chemical reactions
items.origX: Researchers discovered a hidden factor that can determine whether chemical reactions succeed or fail, and then used it to boost the proportion of the desired product from 16% to 97%. By controlling acidity near electrodes, they developed a promising way to manufacture chemicals for plastics, medicines, and other products using oxygen and electricity instead of hazardous added oxidants.

items.t: 大堡礁最臭名昭著的珊瑚殺手可能實際上正在幫助它
items.x: 荆棘冠海星因吞噬珊瑚礁而臭名昭著，但令人惊讶的新研究表明，当这些多刺的捕食者的数量受到控制时，它们实际上可能有助于珊瑚礁的繁荣。研究澳大利亚大堡礁的科学家发现，观察到的海星摄食事件中近 75% 留下了活珊瑚组织，而不是摧毁整个珊瑚群。以 fa 為食
items.orig: The Great Barrier Reef's most notorious coral killer may actually be helping it
items.origX: Crown-of-thorns starfish are notorious for devouring coral reefs, but surprising new research reveals these spiny predators may actually help reefs thrive when their populations are kept in check. Scientists studying Australia's Great Barrier Reef discovered that nearly 75% of observed starfish feeding events left behind living coral tissue, rather than destroying entire colonies. By feeding on fast-growing, dominant corals, the starfish create opportunities for slower-growing species to survive, potentially increasing coral biodiversity.

items.t: 小行星杀死了恐龙。鱷魚為何能存活？
items.x: 科學家可能已經解開了一個 6600 萬年前的謎團：鱷魚如何在滅絕恐龍的小行星中倖存下來。對化石和古代氣候的全面分析表明，它們對溫暖環境的偏好使它們處於熱帶避難所，即使在災難性影響之後，這些避難所仍然適合居住。
items.orig: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?
items.origX: Scientists may have solved a 66-million-year-old mystery: how crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs. A sweeping analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests that their preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that remained habitable even after the catastrophic impact.

items.t: 科學家表示，一個被遺忘的粒子可能會解釋宇宙存在的原因
items.x: 一種被忽視了數十年的神秘粒子可能是解釋物質為何能在大爆炸中倖存下來、讓恆星、行星和生命得以存在的關鍵。科學家認為，這種被遺忘的中微子重塑了早期宇宙，並可能留下了可偵測到的重力波訊號，有助於解開宇宙最深的奧秘。
items.orig: Scientists say a forgotten particle may explain why the universe exists
items.origX: A mysterious particle overlooked for decades may hold the key to why matter survived the Big Bang, allowing stars, planets, and life to exist. Scientists believe this forgotten neutrino reshaped the early universe and may have left detectable gravitational wave signals that could help unlock the cosmos’s deepest mysteries.

items.t: 人工智慧揭示了一種隱藏的化學捷徑，可以將二氧化碳轉化為燃料
items.x: 科學家利用人工智慧發現了近 10,000 個將二氧化碳轉化為燃料和化學品的化學反應，揭示了傳統模型遺漏的關鍵途徑。這項發現極大地改善了對二氧化碳轉化的預測，並揭示了一種令人驚訝的氫反應，可以激發更高效的催化劑。
items.orig: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.origX: Scientists used artificial intelligence to uncover nearly 10,000 chemical reactions involved in transforming carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals, revealing crucial pathways that traditional models had missed. The discovery dramatically improved predictions of CO2 conversion and uncovered a surprising hydrogen reaction that could inspire more efficient catalysts.

items.t: 埃及的古猿化石可能改寫人類起源的故事
items.x: 在埃及發現的一個 1700 至 1800 萬年前的猿類化石正在挑戰人們長期以來對人類和其他現代猿類祖先最初進化地點的看法。科學家現在懷疑北非和中東，而不是東非，可能是現代猿類進化的搖籃。
items.orig: Ancient ape fossil in Egypt could rewrite the story of human origins
items.origX: A 17- to 18-million-year-old ape fossil discovered in Egypt is challenging long-held beliefs about where the ancestors of humans and other modern apes first evolved. Scientists now suspect that North Africa and the Middle East, rather than East Africa, may have been the cradle of modern ape evolution.
